properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored CryptoJS RC4 stream-cipher implementation bundled inside the web3.js console dependency (internal/jsre/deps/web3.js), shipped in every geth binary that serves the JS console. No application call site in this repo, but the implementation is present and reachable by any console script via CryptoJS.RC4. RC4 is cryptographically broken (biases, no key separation). Changeable here only by pruning/rebuilding the vendored web3.js bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored CryptoJS TripleDES implementation inside the bundled web3.js console dependency. 3DES is deprecated (112-bit effective strength) and quantum-irrelevant for PQ migration but a weak classical cipher. Reachable by console scripts via CryptoJS.TripleDES; no application call site in this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Engine-API (CL↔EL) JWT authentication in geth's node package. Claims validation is deliberately switched off per the Ethereum engine API spec: the server is only required to check the HS256 signature against the shared secret; claims such as exp are optional. The effective control is HMAC-SHA256 (see ALG-c6eac685) with a 120-bit randomly generated secret (node/jwt_handler.go genJWTSecret). Signature verification itself is NOT disabled — this is the standard, conformant configuration for the exec

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored CryptoJS HmacMD5 implementation inside the bundled web3.js console dependency. MD5-based MAC; collision-broken underlying hash. No application call site in this repo; reachable by console scripts.

The 5578 sites span the Go wrappers, the vendored C implementation (crypto/secp256k1/libsecp256k1, 101 objects of its own), tests and the fuzzers. properties.value: AES-CTR as the Web3 Secret Storage v3 cipher ("aes-128-ctr" written into new keystores at passphrase.go:172 and enforced on decrypt at :244) and presale wallet decryption (presale.go:113). Unauthenticated by spec design — v3 keystores rely on the scrypt/PBKDF2 KDF rather than a MAC. Remaining sites are the shipped v1/v3 test vectors. Spec-fixed format; changeable only via a new keystore version.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Unauthenticated AES-CBC in two production paths: presale wallet key blobs (accounts/keystore/presale.go:124 — aes-128-cbc decrypt of the legacy 2014 presale format) and the status-card secure channel (accounts/scwallet/securechannel.go:283/309/337 — CBC encrypt/decrypt plus zero-IV CBC-MAC for channel authentication). Plus the v1 keystore test vector. CBC here is interoperability-fixed: the presale format and the smartcard channel spec cannot be changed unilaterally.

These are the account-key generation paths: keystore account creation (key.go:155/167), the central crypto.GenerateKey (crypto/crypto.go:235), ECIES keygen (ecies.go:100) and a secp256k1 test. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored CryptoJS HmacSHA1 implementation inside the bundled web3.js console dependency. SHA-1 is collision-broken; the MAC is only Grover-weakened, but the primitive is deprecated. No application call site in this repo; reachable from console scripts.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Engine-API (CL↔EL) JWT authentication pins jwt.WithValidMethods([]string{"HS256"}) in node/jwt_handler.go: HMAC-SHA256 over a shared secret that geth generates at 120 random bits when the operator does not supply --authrpc.jwtsecret. HMAC-SHA256 is quantum-adequate (Grover-only weakening); the operative risks are secret distribution and the deliberately disabled claims validation (ALG-07035178), not the MAC.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Production use is the secp256r1 verify EVM precompile: core/vm/contracts.go:1639 calls secp256r1.Verify(hash,r,s,x,y) via the in-tree crypto/secp256r1 package, exposing NIST P-256 ECDSA verification to smart contracts. The other ~200 sites are wycheproof conformance vectors in core/vm/testdata/precompiles/p256Verify.json plus the precompile's tests. Shor-vulnerable signature verification; the precompile set is consensus-fixed — replaceable only through an EIP.

properties.value: All 7 sites are real outbound HTTPS sessions made with net/http default settings (matched via the shared "go-https-client" User-Agent): beacon light-client API calls (beacon/light/api/light_api.go:117), the devp2p ethtest engine harness, and RPC client tests. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto/signify implements OpenBSD signify-format signing with Ed25519: signify.go:81 signs the file data, :91 signs the comment, over the ed25519 private key. Shor-vulnerable signature scheme; the format itself fixes Ed25519 for signify interoperability, so replacement means dropping the format, not swapping the curve.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Positive posture control, not a weakness: crypto/ecies/ecies.go:325 verifies ECIES MACs with constant-time comparison (subtle-style), preventing the timing oracle on plaintext validity. Recorded as a control the inventory should keep.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Remaining sites are real: crypto/ecies/params.go registers ECIES parameter sets for the NIST curves (elliptic.P384(): ECIES_AES192_SHA384, P521: AES256_SHA512) and crypto/ecies/ecies_test.go:278-284 exercises those curves — the ECIES registry supports P-384/P-521 for interoperability even though the default curve is secp256k1. Shor-vulnerable EC key agreement if those parameter sets are used.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (the pre-standardization Keccak that Ethereum fixed, via x/crypto/sha3) is the consensus hash: transaction/header hashes, Merkle-Patricia-trie node hashing, address derivation, ABI encoding, RLPx frame MACs, and the SHA3 precompile (0x02→Keccak256) offered to contracts. Quantum posture is the best of the assets here: Grover halves preimage strength, no Shor break; and it is consensus/protocol-fixed — changing it is a network redesign, not a repo change.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 in supporting roles: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 for keystore/presale key derivation (accounts/keystore), the HMAC-SHA256 JWT for the engine API, era-file download checksums, the p256Verify precompile's hashing, and scwallet derivations. Quantum-adequate (Grover only).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Password-based key derivation for keystore decryption, two paths: the Web3 Secret Storage "pbkdf2" branch (passphrase.go:346/352 — PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with the iteration count read from the keystore JSON; classic vectors are in the tens of thousands, far below the 600k OWASP minimum) and the legacy 2014 presale wallet format (presale.go), hard-frozen at 2000 PBKDF2 rounds (presale.go:79) — trivially brute-forceable offline; the only mitigation is that the format is legacy. Quantum-adequate hash family (Grover only), consensus-fixed as a precompile.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128 as the keystore v3 cipher key size (aes-128-ctr derived from scrypt/PBKDF2), the presale format (aes-128-ctr/cbc), and the scwallet secure channel (AES-128 session keys). Quantum: Grover halves 128-bit to 64-bit search for the recorded-traffic case — adequate for the threat model, weak modes tracked separately.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Scrypt as the Web3 Secret Storage v3 default KDF: geth writes N=262144 (2^18), r=8, p=1 for new keystores (accounts/keystore/passphrase.go:145 scrypt.Key; params stored in and enforced from the keystore JSON). Memory-hard, quantum-adequate. Old low-parameter files are decryptable but that is file-driven, not a code default.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Authenticated encryption in two production paths: discv5 node communication (p2p/discover/v5wire/crypto.go — AES-GCM with HKDF-SHA256-derived session keys after secp256k1 ECDH) and clef's credential storage (signer/storage/aes_gcm_storage.go — AES-GCM for stored secrets). Quantum-adequate AE (AES-256-GCM in discv5 keying); the quantum exposure is the ECDH that feeds it, tracked as ALG-c9ffc8a8.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC over SHA-256-or-stronger: the scwallet secure-channel MAC (accounts/scwallet) and the vendored crypto-js HMAC-SHA256 inside the web3.js console bundle (internal/jsre/deps/web3.js:11220). Quantum-adequate MACs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HKDF-SHA256 expanding discv5 handshake ECDH output into the wire session keys (p2p/discover/v5wire/crypto.go:128), plus the golang.org/x/crypto/hkdf dependency of the cmd/keeper module. Quantum-adequate KDF; the quantum exposure is the upstream ECDH.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 integrity checksums for released artifacts (build/checksums.txt) and downloaded era files (internal/era/eradl/checksums_mainnet.txt) — integrity control, not a security boundary against attackers who control the download source; quantum-adequate.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ANSI X9.63 concatenation KDF inside geth's ECIES (crypto/ecies/ecies.go:172) deriving the AES/HMAC keys from the secp256k1 shared point — used by the RLPx handshake and the eth `eth_decryptMessage`-style paths. Quantum-adequate KDF itself; the Shor exposure is the secp256k1 ECDH feeding it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-384/SHA-512 in the smart-card wallet paths (accounts/scwallet: secure-channel key derivation and MACs, wallet.go:930) — the status-card protocol fixes these digests. Quantum-adequate (Grover only).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-256 as the ECIES parameter set for non-secp256k1 curves (crypto/ecies/params.go:100 AES256-SHA512 params registry) exercised by ecies_test.go:285; also the AES-256-GCM discv5 keying. Quantum-adequate.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto/rand.Reader is the randomness source for every security-relevant choice sampled: account key generation (crypto.GenerateKey, keystore), ECIES ephemeral keys, discv5 handshake material, JWT secret generation. The right primitive; PRNG security is unaffected by Shor/Grover in any practical way. This object is the healthy counterpart to the math/rand sites grouped under ALG-7d1fdc12.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Module-graph references to the JWT signing libraries backing node/jwt_handler.go: github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4 (actively maintained) with the superseded dgrijalva/jwt-go still recorded in go.sum. The signing algorithm in use is HS256/HMAC-SHA256 (see ALG-c6eac685); no RS/ES tokens are minted by this code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The well-known OpenSSL "rsa-testing-key" PEM block, present as fuzz-corpus seed inputs for the txfetcher fuzzer (tests/fuzzers/txfetcher/corpus). Test data only — it authenticates nothing and guards nothing; recorded because committed RSA key material, even test material, belongs in a key inventory. RSA itself is Shor-vulnerable, but this key secures no system.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: golang.org/x/crypto is the main module's extended-crypto dependency: sha3 (Keccak-256 consensus hashing), scrypt (keystore v3 KDF), pbkdf2 (keystore/presale KDF), hkdf (discv5 key derivation), ripemd160 (the 0x03 EVM precompile), and openpgp (indirect, pulled via the ZKM zkVM runtime in cmd/keeper). All classical; PQ posture of each tracked under its own object.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pion/dtls/v3 is declared in the main module's go.mod but imported by no Go file in this tree (repo-wide grep for pion/dtls: 0 matches) — a module-graph leftover. If ever linked, pion/dtls v3 offers DTLS 1.2/1.3 with classical ECDHE (X25519/P-256) key exchange only and no post-quantum groups. Recorded as a declared dependency with no call site; removable with a module tidy.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: golang.org/x/crypto as required by the cmd/keeper builder module — pulled indirectly via the ZKM Ziren zkvm_runtime dependency; no direct x/crypto import exists in cmd/keeper's own Go files. The main module's direct x/crypto uses are tracked under their own objects (sha3/Keccak, scrypt, pbkdf2, hkdf, ripemd160).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp is required (indirectly) by the cmd/keeper module via the ZKM zkvm_runtime chain. That implementation is deprecated upstream and its defaults are weak (3DES-era cipher suites, RSA/DSA keys); no direct call site exists in this tree — the exposure is that the module graph still carries it. Observable here only as a dependency edge.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Committed 32-byte private key file used as testdata by the geth CLI account tests (cmd/geth/testdata/key.prv). Test material, not production: it is a secp256k1-format account key fed to account-import paths under test. Secures nothing; kept in the inventory as committed key material with its purpose recorded.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The maintained github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4 backs node/jwt_handler.go's HS256 engine-API authentication (see ALG-c6eac685). HMAC-SHA256 tokens; quantum-adequate MAC, Grover only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The original github.com/dgrijalva/jwt-go — archived upstream and carrying CVE-2020-26160 (audience validation) — persists only in go.sum; no import in the tree references it. Recorded so the stale module-graph reference is visible; the maintained golang-jwt/v4 is what the code actually uses.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The same pion/dtls/v3 dependency as ALG-166cbbb4, identified by package name rather than protocol name: declared in go.mod, zero imports in the tree, classical-ECDHE-only DTLS 1.2/1.3 stack if ever linked. One logical asset under two names.

properties.name: pqs:context
